dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:9701.text: The central palace. It depicts all things opening, storing away, and bending. 己 follows 戊 and depicts a person's abdomen. All characters in this group are formed from 己.

shuowen:9702.text: To conduct oneself carefully while receiving something. Formed from 己 and 丞. Read like 己 in the Odes' 'Red shoes, steady and dignified.'

shuowen:9703.text: To sit long with legs spread. Formed from 己, with 其 indicating the sound. Read like 杞.

shuowen:9704.text: A creature. Some say a snake that eats elephants. A pictograph. All characters in this group are formed from 巴.

shuowen:9705.text: To strike backhanded. Formed from 巴 and 帚; further explanation is lacking.

shuowen:9706.text: Its position is in the west, depicting all things in autumn firm and substantial. 庚 follows 己 and depicts a person's 𪗇, apparently the navel. All characters in this group are formed from 庚.

shuowen:9707.text: In autumn all things mature and ripen; metal is hard, the flavor acrid, and acrid pain brings tears. Formed from 一 and 䇂. 䇂 means an offense. 辛 follows 庚 and depicts a person's thighs. All characters in this group are formed from 辛.

shuowen:9708.text: To break the law. Formed from 辛 and 自, expressing the offender's wrinkled nose and bitter, painful distress. Qin changed it to 罪 because 辠 resembled 皇.

shuowen:9709.text: An offense. Formed from 辛, with 古 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9710.text: An offense. Formed from 辛, with 𡴎 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9711.text: Not to accept. Formed from 辛 and 受: when receiving hardship, one should decline it.

shuowen:9712.text: To litigate. Formed from 𤔔, which is like adjudicating offenses. 𤔔 means to put in order.

shuowen:9713.text: Offenders litigating with one another. Formed from two 辛. All characters in this group are formed from 辡.

shuowen:9714.text: To adjudicate or put in order. Formed from 言 between the two 辛 of 辡.

shuowen:9715.text: Its position is in the north. Yin reaches its utmost and yang is born; thus the Changes says: 'Dragons fight in the fields.' Fighting means joining. It depicts a person carrying a pregnancy. Following 亥, 壬 is succeeded by 子, the sequence of birth. The same conception as 巫. 壬 follows 辛 and depicts a person's shins, which support the body. All characters in this group are formed from 壬.

shuowen:9716.text: In winter water and earth are level and can be measured. It depicts water flowing from four directions into the earth. 癸 follows 壬 and depicts a person's feet. All characters in this group are formed from 癸.

shuowen:9717.text: In the eleventh month yang vital energy moves and all things increase; people use this term for it. A pictograph. All characters in this group are formed from 子. Li Yangbing says: 'A child in swaddling clothes, with feet together.'

shuowen:9718.text: To carry a child in the womb. Formed from 子 and 几.

shuowen:9719.text: To give birth and free the body. Formed from 子 and 免.

shuowen:9720.text: To bear or nurture a child. Formed from 子 beneath 宀; 子 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:9721.text: To bear or nurse a child. Formed from 子, with 𣪊 indicating the sound. Alternatively, the condition expressed by 㝅瞀.

shuowen:9722.text: Two children from one birth. Formed from 子, with 䜌 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9723.text: A nursing child. Alternatively, 輸, explained as still small. Formed from 子, with 需 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9724.text: A designation for the youngest. Formed from 子 and abbreviated 稚; 稚 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:9725.text: The eldest. Formed from 子, with 皿 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9726.text: A secondary wife's son. Formed from 子, with 辥 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9727.text: To bring forth assiduously. Formed from 子, with 兹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9728.text: Without a father. Formed from 子, with 瓜 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9729.text: To care for and inquire after. Formed from 子, with 才 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9730.text: To release or let go. Formed from 子, with 爻 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9731.text: Doubt or confusion. Formed from 子, 止, and 匕, with 矢 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9732.text: Bent or intertwined, as in 尦. Formed from 子 without arms; a pictograph. All characters in this group are formed from 了.

shuowen:9733.text: Without a right arm. Formed from 了, with 乚 depicting the shape.

shuowen:9734.text: Without a left arm. Formed from 了, with 丿 depicting the shape.

shuowen:9735.text: Careful. Formed from three 子. All characters in this group are formed from 孨. Read like 翦.

shuowen:9736.text: Cramped. Alternatively, groaning. Formed from 孨 beneath 尸.

shuowen:9737.text: An abundant appearance. Formed from 孨 and 曰. Read like 薿 in 薿薿; alternatively, like 存.

shuowen:9738.text: To emerge suddenly and disobediently. Formed from reversed 子. The Changes says: 'Suddenly it comes.' An unfilial child bursts out, not accommodated within. All characters in this group are formed from 𠫓.

shuowen:9739.text: To rear children so that they do good. Formed from 𠫓, with 肉 indicating the sound. The Book of Yu says: 'Teach and rear the children.'

shuowen:9740.text: To pass through. Formed from 𡿮 and 疋; 疋 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:9741.text: A bond or knot. In the twelfth month all things stir and begin their work. It depicts a hand. When the time reaches 丑, it is also time to raise the hands. All characters in this group are formed from 丑.

shuowen:9742.text: To eat meat. Formed from 丑 and 肉.

shuowen:9743.text: To present an offering. Formed from 羊, the thing presented, and 丑; 丑 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:9744.text: Constrained, as in 髕. In the first month yang vital energy stirs and leaves the Yellow Springs, wanting to emerge upward; yin remains strong. It depicts being unable to pass through 宀, constrained below. All characters in this group are formed from 寅.

shuowen:9745.text: To emerge or cover. In the second month all things push through the earth and emerge. It depicts an open gate; hence the second month is Heaven's Gate. All characters in this group are formed from 卯.

shuowen:9746.text: To shake. In the third month yang vital energy stirs, thunder and lightning shake, and it is the people's farming season. All things grow: 乙 and 匕 depict shoots coming through; 厂 indicates the sound. 辰 is the 房 star, a heavenly seasonal marker. Includes 二, ancient-script 上. All characters in this group are formed from 辰.

shuowen:9747.text: Disgrace. Formed from 寸 below 辰. Those who miss plowing time are punished at the territorial boundary. 辰 is the farming season; hence the 房 star is 辰, the fields' seasonal marker.

shuowen:9748.text: Already or completed. In the fourth month yang vital energy has emerged and yin has hidden; all things appear and develop patterned forms. Thus 巳 represents a snake; a pictograph. All characters in this group are formed from 巳.

shuowen:9749.text: To use. Formed from reversed 巳. Palace Attendant Jia says: 巳 conveys already full or substantial. A pictograph.

shuowen:9750.text: To oppose. In the fifth month yin vital energy opposes yang and emerges through the earth. The same conception as 予 and 矢. All characters in this group are formed from 午.

shuowen:9751.text: To oppose. Formed from 午, with 吾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9752.text: Flavor. In the sixth month flavors develop. Among the five phases, wood grows old at 未. It depicts a tree with repeated branches and leaves. All characters in this group are formed from 未.

shuowen:9753.text: Divine or spiritual. In the seventh month yin vital energy takes form, and bodies draw in and constrain themselves. Formed from 臼, holding itself. Officials hear business at the afternoon meal and renew the morning's governance; the source records 吏臣, with Duan's note changing 臣 to 以. All characters in this group are formed from 申.

shuowen:9754.text: To strike a small drum and lead the musical sound. Formed from 申, with 柬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9755.text: Being bound, seized, and dragged is called 臾. Formed from 申 and 乙.

shuowen:9756.text: The dragging expressed by 臾曳. Formed from 申, with 丿 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9757.text: To complete. In the eighth month millet matures and can make repeatedly brewed wine. It depicts the ancient-script 酉. All characters in this group are formed from 酉.

shuowen:9758.text: To bring to completion: that which brings out the good and evil of human nature. Formed from 水 and 酉; 酉 also indicates the sound. Alternatively, to bring about, since good and ill arise from it. In antiquity Yidi made fermented liquor; Yu tasted it and found it good, then distanced Yidi. Du Kang made glutinous-grain wine.

shuowen:9759.text: Fermenting grain growing a coating. Formed from 酉, with 冡 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9760.text: Ripened fermenting grain. Formed from 酉, with 甚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9761.text: To ferment: making wine is called 釀. Formed from 酉, with 襄 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9762.text: To brew or ferment. Formed from 酉, with 𥁕 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9763.text: Wine ripening quickly. Formed from 酉, with 弁 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9764.text: The starter of wine. Formed from 酉, with 余 indicating the sound. Read like 廬.

shuowen:9765.text: To draw off wine. Alternatively, unadulterated wine. Formed from 酉, with 麗 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9766.text: To strain wine. Formed from 酉, with 肙 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9767.text: To strain wine. Formed from 酉, with 鬲 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9768.text: Wine ripened in one night. Formed from 酉, with 豊 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9769.text: Wine containing liquid and dregs. Formed from 酉, with 翏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9770.text: Wine that has not been diluted. Formed from 酉, with 𦎫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9771.text: Rich, thick wine. Formed from 酉, with 需 indicating the sound. The Odes says: 'Wine and sweet wine are rich.'

shuowen:9772.text: Unadulterated wine brewed three times. Formed from 酉 and abbreviated 時. The Bright Hall's Monthly Ordinances says: 'In the first autumn month the Son of Heaven drinks 酎.'

shuowen:9773.text: Turbid wine. Formed from 酉, with 盎 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9774.text: Rich, thick wine. Formed from 酉, with 農 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9775.text: Wine. Formed from 酉, with 茸 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9776.text: Wine made in one night. Alternatively, to buy wine. Formed from 酉, with 古 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9777.text: Wine. Formed from 酉 and abbreviated 𥏼.

shuowen:9778.text: The floating fermentation grade, 泛齊; wine in use or circulation, as recorded by 行酒. Formed from 酉, with 監 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9779.text: Wine flavor being excessive or rich. Formed from 酉, with abbreviated 竷 indicating the sound. Read like 豔 in the Spring and Autumn Commentary's 'Beautiful and alluring.'

shuowen:9780.text: A rich flavor of wine. Formed from 酉, with 告 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9781.text: Wine tasting bitter. Formed from 酉, with 覃 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9782.text: The color of wine. Formed from 酉, with 巿 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9783.text: The color of wine. Formed from 酉, with 己 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9784.text: The color of wine. Formed from 酉, with 弋 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9785.text: A wine cup. Alternatively, wine turbid but slightly clear. Formed from 酉, with 戔 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9786.text: To fill wine and pass the cup. Formed from 酉, with 勺 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9787.text: A sacrifice in the capping and marriage rites. Formed from 酉, with 焦 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9788.text: To sip wine. Formed from 酉, with 朁 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9789.text: To drink little by little. Formed from 酉, with 勻 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9790.text: The host offering wine to the guest. Formed from 酉, with 𠷎 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9791.text: The guest pouring wine for the host. Formed from 酉, with 昔 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9792.text: To drink wine and finish it together. Formed from 酉, with 𥁑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9793.text: To finish drinking the wine. Formed from 酉, with abbreviated 嚼 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9794.text: To enjoy wine. Formed from 酉 and 甘; 甘 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:9795.text: To delight in wine. Formed from 酉, with 冘 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9796.text: To drink at a private banquet. Formed from 酉, with 區 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9797.text: To gather together to drink wine. Formed from 酉, with 豦 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9798.text: The king's virtue being spread abroad through a great public drinking feast. Formed from 酉, with 甫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9799.text: Drunk and full. Formed from 酉, with 咅 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9800.text: To finish: to complete one's measured allowance without reaching disorder. Alternatively, to collapse. Formed from 酉 and 卒.
